text:
Every Thursday at 3:12, Mara finds the same book in the bread rack. It's the practical guide to inland birds, blue spine cracked, library stamp from a town forty miles away. She puts it on the flour bin, wipes the butter off the cover, and means to return it after her shift. But by noon, the errands, the heat, the sleep, and other things swallow it. Next Thursday it's there, tucked between cooling rye loaves.
Tonight the bakery hums. The proofing cabinet runs, and the radio sits in static. Rain leaves silver lines on the front window. She picks up the book with both hands, as if it might be warm. A folded receipt marks the chapter on herons. She opens it. Block letters read: I THINK YOU ARE THE ONLY PERSON AWAKE WHEN I AM. Page 47.
She turns to 47. Grey heron in a marsh, one foot raised, patient as a saint. Under it, in pencil: THURSDAY, 3:30? The clock over the mixer clicks once. She brushes flour off her apron, unlocks the front door, and turns on the little OPEN sign.
